title: Ephemeral arena surge: KV shadow-spill rebuild + OOM fallback operator
creator: Asha Patel
description: Multiple customer escalations across Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments have surfaced an emergent failure mode that causes repeated GPU OOMs during short, high-concurrency bursts. Symptoms: sudden spike in per-session arena consumption, rapid growth of KV-index tombstones ('shadow-spill'), and allocator fragmentation that prevents compact reclaiming. Impacted pathways include hosted burst traffic (short-lived but high-QPS), Dedicated multi-tenant nodes running mixed-sequence workloads, and on-prem Private installs where compaction cron can't keep pace. Root cause hypothesis: concurrent eviction + index tombstone accumulation triggers asynchronous spill-to-disk and a thrash loop in the ephemeral arena allocator; while background compaction is single-threaded and scheduled under low priority, it cannot keep up, causing transient address-space starvation on GPU and subsequent OOMs. This ticket scopes: 1) emergency mitigations to stabilize live clusters and protect customers, 2) a runtime patch implementing bounded async compaction + preemptive arena backpressure, and 3) rollout + verification plan (canary -> staged) and follow-up postmortem.
comments: 2025-03-02 - Incident triage: SE on-call alerted after 2 Hosted customers reported repeated generation failures and OOM traces. Initial mitigation applied: tenant-rate-limit increase + temporary model fallback for the affected routes. Noted similar stack traces from a Dedicated customer (internal ticket ref: PM-987).

2025-03-03 - Reproduced locally with stress harness (multi-session mixed lengths). Observed KV index tombstone growth when eviction/compact windows overlapped; arena free lists fractured under concurrent alloc/free. Filed instrumentation PR to add allocator histograms and tombstone-rate metrics (GH PR: https://github.com/redwood/realtime/pull/4973).

2025-03-04 - Short-term mitigations deployed to Hosted: (a) enable 'oom-fallback-operator' that preemptively reroutes requests to compatible lower-memory model variant when arena utilization > 72%; (b) rate-limit bursty tenants for 10s buckets. Early telemetry shows 65% reduction in OOM retry rate in canary region eu-west-1.

2025-03-06 - Engineering design review: agreed on two-part runtime patch: (1) bounded asynchronous compaction per KV-shard with dynamic worker pool, and (2) a session-level arena backpressure gate that rejects/queues requests rather than letting allocator fragment further. Trade-offs discussed: compaction workers increase CPU and IO during heavy churn; backpressure may increase tail latency. Decided to prioritize availability with transparent fallbacks and instrumented observability.

2025-03-07 - Security/ops note: Private customers with air-gapped installs require an offline patch bundle. Work to coordinate release artifacts and migration steps was assigned to infra-ops (owner: Maria Ruiz).

2025-03-09 - Implementation progress: compaction worker prototype merged behind feature flag (GH PR: https://github.com/redwood/realtime/pull/5021). Added metrics: kv.tombstone_rate, allocator.fragmentation_ratio, arena.utilization_percent. Unit + integration tests added to CI harness (jobs/runtime-stability).

2025-03-10 - Canary rollout: enabled feature flag in 2 Hosted canaries, and enabled oom-fallback-operator globally for Hosted while compaction remains behind flag. Observed KV tombstone drain rate improvement (median drain latency down 4x) and lower fragmentation slope. One Dedicated cluster reported mild CPU spike from compaction workers; autoscaler adjusted policy to add temporary CPU nodes in that pool.

2025-03-11 - Customer comms: notified impacted customers with status update and mitigation steps; offered post-incident follow-up and optional deep-dive call. Logged incident channel: https://slack.redwood.ai/incidents/arena-surge-2025-03.

2025-03-12 - Next actions: finish stress tests for worst-case tenant isolation, prepare Private/offline patch bundle, file postmortem and bake compaction tuning recommendations into Optimize heuristics. Plan to flip feature flag in additional regions after 48h observation window.
